item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
First of all, thank you for taking the time to read my Tale, I'm happy it was easy enough to read for you! And for your questions and interrogations, here's some answers.

there isn't much that gets advanced here that couldn't be covered in a paragraph of a longer tale. Bowe is a no-nonsense kind of guy in the mold of every high-ranking white military officer with a grey crewcut from every movie ever. He's asking a monster of some kind to join his cause.

Technically, "Him" is not really a monster, at least in the way I depict him. He's more like the "It's a person who wants to do good, but are not really aware that they also fuck up a lot of things" type. Plus, in my original idea for the Tale (I don't know for now if I will involve more explicitly this idea), "Him" was supposed to be more silently skeptical towards Bowe and his allies but join them only because he thought he could reach his own goals.

But because of an increasing stress and dissatisfaction with what I was doing, I've scrapped the idea of a more longer Tale and my teammates help me for turning the draft into something I could be satisfied!

I feel like there's some characterization or important context that I am missing from not being familiar with 093

There's some references to the "Recovered Materials" article at the beginning, but the characterization of "Him" is entirely mine. There's not many Tales who feature the character, so it was perfect for me in order to give him more personality.

That don't make your concerns less valid, but I hope these answers make it more clear!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Jesus, this reminds me of 093, specifically how I still haven't read it after almost a decade here. Might as well lean into it and make it my thing.

As for the tale itself, it's fine? There are some prose bits that stick out like a sore thumb ("Not the "oh-dear-God-why-we're-all-screwed-they're-too-much-life-seems-so-meaningless-all-of-a-sudden" kind of surprised"), but it is an easy enough read.

The problem is that there isn't much that gets advanced here that couldn't be covered in a paragraph of a longer tale. Bowe is a no-nonsense kind of guy in the mold of every high-ranking white military officer with a grey crewcut from every movie ever. He's asking a monster of some kind to join his cause. Given that he's already gotten two death cults to do the same, this isn't really a surprise.

I hope that this team manages to avoid one of the problems that made the original Rezz canon such a drag: that there was a significant amount of time devoted to tales that only covered the introduction of a single character, usually utilizing the same framework, which made it just kind of a slog to get through.

I feel like there's some characterization or important context that I am missing from not being familiar with 093, so I'm inclined to no-vote. But yeah, this didn't do much for me.
